raw_response:
Ai-ya, another year, another planting season. Let me think through everything before I decide.

---

I'm 56 this year. My husband and I have been working this land since we got married — 35 years now. Our son works in the city, sends some money when he can but not much. So it's really just me and my husband in the fields, and sometimes my daughter-in-law helps when she's back from town. My hands aren't as fast as they used to be, and my back hurts after a day of weeding. But this is what I know.

We have 14 mu all together. It's not all in one piece — the pieces are scattered. The best 8 mu near the village, the flat ones, I do wheat-maize there like my mother-in-law taught me. One after the other, no rest for the land. That's how we feed ourselves and have grain to sell. Then there's 5 mu further out, sandier soil, where I grow cotton. Cotton is hard work but the price has been okay, and on that sandy land wheat doesn't do as well anyway. And I keep 1 mu of chili near the house — that's my money crop. My neighbor Wang Sao has been growing chili for years and she helps me sell to the trader who comes through.

---

**The wheat** (8 mu) — Last October I planted the same variety as always, the one the seed store sells, "Jimai something" (济麦), I don't remember the number. My husband bought four packets, about 15 kg per mu of seed — maybe a bit more because late planting, you need thicker stand. Before planting we put down compound fertilizer, one bag per mu, that's the 15-15-15 kind. Then when the wheat starts jointing in April, I'll spread urea — about half a bag per mu, maybe a bit more if the leaves look pale. That's what Wang Sao's husband does and their wheat always looks good.

For water — we have the well, but the electricity for pumping isn't cheap. Last year I watered three times: once after sowing because autumn was dry, once at the green-up in spring, and once at grain-filling. I'll probably do the same this year. If it rains good I'll skip one. For pests, I don't spray much. Maybe once in spring for the weeds — 2,4-D, the old stuff, cheap. Aphids if they come. My wheat should give me around 450 kg per mu, maybe more if the spring rain comes.

**The maize** (8 mu) — Right after wheat harvest in June, you have to hurry. Maybe a week at most to get maize in. I hire the neighbor with the no-till planter — 30 yuan per mu, he does it in an afternoon. I buy Zhengdan 958 seed, or whatever hybrid the store has that year, about 2-3 kg per mu. I throw some compound fertilizer with the planter, then topdress urea at the big-trumpet stage (大喇叭口期), that's when the plant has about 10-12 leaves, my mother-in-law always said "when the leaves are like a trumpet, feed it." Maybe half a bag of urea per mu.

Maize doesn't need much water if the summer rain comes. Usually I only irrigate once, at tasseling, if it's been dry. For pests — maybe one spray for armyworm if I see damage. My maize usually gives 500 kg per mu, sometimes 550 in a good year.

**The cotton** (5 mu) — Cotton is the hard one. I plant mid-April when the soil warms up. I use seed from the local cotton company, they sell treated seed. We do some tillage in March to break the soil. Base fertilizer, I put one bag of compound per mu, mostly because cotton grows long. Then I topdress urea twice — once at squaring, once at flowering, about half a bag each time. My husband does the spraying, because cotton needs spraying many times — for bollworm, mirids, aphids. Maybe 6-7 sprays through the season, that's a lot of money on pesticide but if you don't spray, you lose everything.

Irrigation — cotton needs water at flowering especially. I do it twice usually, from the well. Picking is the hardest — three or four pickings from September through October. I do most of it myself, my husband helps on weekends. Sometimes I ask my sister to come help for a few days, I give her some cotton in return. I expect maybe 250 kg lint per mu, if the weather is okay and the bollworm doesn't get bad.

**The chili** (1 mu) — This is my special crop. I start seedlings in a small plot in March, transplant in May. Wang Sao gave me advice on the variety — the long thin red one that goes to the trader. Chili needs lots of fertilizer and water. I put a lot of farmyard manure from our goats in winter, then compound fertilizer at transplanting, then I topdress several times with urea and sometimes with potassium — Wang Sao told me the peppers get bigger with potassium. I spray for anthracnose when the rain comes, that disease can ruin the whole crop.

Chili is labor — weeding, staking, picking every few days in August-September. I do it myself, my hands are used to it. But the price is good if the market is good — last year I made nearly 3000 yuan from that one mu alone, more than three mu of maize. This year I'll try the same.

---

My biggest worries: cash. I already bought the fertilizer for wheat topdress and the cotton inputs — borrowed 1000 yuan from my brother. I need to pay him back after maize harvest. Pesticide cost for cotton keeps going up. And my knees — I don't know how many more years I can pick cotton by hand.
